name: rag-survey-2312.10997
field: Retrieval-augmented generation for large language models

brief.topics: RAG pipelines, retrieval quality, hallucination reduction, RAG vs fine-tuning
brief.background: Strong in machine learning and Python; some NLP; no lab compute beyond a single GPU
brief.compute_data: One 24 GB GPU; public QA and retrieval benchmarks
brief.timeline: About 3 years left; wants 2 conference papers

provenance: Full text of section VII (Discussion and Future Prospects) read via https://arxiv.org/html/2312.10997 with a summarizing fetch tool, so the wording below is paraphrased, not verbatim. arXiv API metadata checked 2026-10-28 (version v5, 2024-03-27).

known_gaps.text: RAG versus long-context LLMs: retrieval still matters for speed, on-demand input and verifiable sourcing as context windows grow
Robustness of RAG to noisy or contradictory retrieved information and to adversarial inputs
Hybrid approaches that combine RAG with fine-tuning, including how to sequence or jointly train them
Scaling laws for RAG are uncertain; smaller RAG models may outperform larger ones
Production-ready RAG: efficiency, recall at scale and data security remain open engineering problems
Multi-modal RAG that retrieves over images, audio, video and code
